Kuvitus: satama ylhäältä katsottuna. Ylä: Illustration: the harbour seen from above. In the upper part is the open sea, where wave crests travel in straight rows towards the shore. A breakwater made of rocks crosses the picture, and in the middle of it there is a narrow gap. Behind the gap, in the harbour basin, the wave crests are arcs that reach all the way to the corners of the basin. There are boats at the quays, and the boat in the corner rocks on the waves.
Kaavakuva kahdesta aallosta ylhäältä kat: Diagram of two waves seen from above. On the left a plane wave: the wavefronts are parallel straight lines spaced by the wavelength lambda, and the rays are arrows perpendicular to them. On the right a circular wave from a point source: the wavefronts are concentric circles, and the rays leave the source in every direction, perpendicular to the fronts.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: köyden puls: Diagram, not to scale: reflection of a rope pulse in two cases. On the left the end of the rope is tied to a wall (fixed end), on the right the end is a ring that slides without friction along a vertical rod (free end). In the top row, before reflection, an upward pulse travels to the right towards the end. In the bottom row, after reflection, the pulse travels to the left: the pulse reflected from the fixed end is inverted and points downwards, the one reflected from the free end still points upwards.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: tasoaalto t: Diagram, not to scale: a plane wave arrives from the left at an obstacle with a slit, seen from above. On the left the slit is about four wavelengths wide: at the slit the wavefronts continue straight, and only at the edges do they curve slightly into the shadow. Small Huygens wavelets are drawn at points of the slit. On the right the slit is narrower than the wavelength: behind the slit the wavefronts are semicircles, and the wave spreads over the whole area behind the slit.
Kaavakuva: tuleva säde osuu seinän pinta: Diagram: the incoming ray hits the surface of the wall at point O, and the reflected ray leaves from it. At O the normal of the surface, the line perpendicular to the surface, is drawn with a dashed line. The angle of incidence alpha is the angle between the incoming ray and the normal, and the angle of reflection beta the angle between the reflected ray and the normal; both are 40 degrees. In grey is marked the angle between the ray and the surface, 90 degrees minus alpha, which is not used as the angle of incidence.
Kaavakuva: Huygensin periaate selittää h: Diagram: Huygens' principle explains the law of reflection. The wavefront AB of a plane wave hits the wall obliquely: point A is already at the wall while point B is still some distance away. When B travels along the ray to the wall at point C, the wavelet that started from A has travelled an equal distance, and its radius is equal to the distance BC. A smaller wavelet is also drawn from the midpoint of A and C. The reflected wavefront CD touches the wavelets. The front AB makes the angle alpha with the wall and the front CD the angle beta, and the angles are equal.
